items.title: 9.7.1 Calculating the pH of a buffer

source_refs.note: Topic 9.7.1 with its Interesting Information box and Quick Check 9.4, printed pages 200-201.

blocks.text: Let us try to learn, how a buffer of definite pH can be prepared. Consider a weak acid HA and its salt NaA with a strong base say NaOH. The reversible reactions for dissociation of HA and NaA are as follows:

blocks.text_alt: HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻; NaA ⇌ Na⁺ + A⁻

This relationship is called Henderson’s equation. This equation shows that two factors evidently govern the pH of a buffer solution. First is the pKa of the acid used and the second is the ratio of the concentrations of the salt and the acid. The best buffer is prepared by taking equal concentration of salt and acid. blocks.text: It means that the pH of this buffer is just equal to the pKa of the acid.
